# song-mv
**English** · 简体中文

Give it a song and an `.lrc` and it draws a beat-synced video, one frame at a
time, on a canvas. Lyr
ics are typography, not a subtitle bar.

What the video looks like is a decision you make, not a default you inherit.
A **look** picks the co

lour world, a small set of **elements** builds the
imagery, and every shot declares a **camera move*

* and an **event** — so the
result moves like a film instead of holding like a poster.

A song about a paper boat gets paper, rain, and a boat that crosses the frame;
it does not get an of

g about a paper boat gets paper, rain, and a boat that crosses the frame;
it does not get an office.
| the same shot, seven looks | |
|  | One `field`/`water` shot with the same lyric in each colour world. Only the look changes. |

Two ways to run it. As a DSH plugin, so you can just ask your agent for a video.
Or as a CLI, if you
'd rather drive it yourself.

**▶ 54 s demo (webm, silent)** · contact sheet

*Frames from the demo. Every pixel is drawn by code — no footage, no images, no
bundled fonts. The a

udio is synthesised by ffmpeg and the lyrics were written for
this repo; see `examples/synthetic-dem

is synthesised by ffmpeg and the lyrics were written for
this repo; see `examples/synthetic-demo`.*

About the test songs: this was built and tuned against commercial tracks I bought
on NetEase Cloud M

usic, together with their `.lrc` files. Those recordings, their
lyrics and the videos rendered from

them are not in this repo. What's here is the
engine, the storyboard format and the synthetic demo.

A frame is a pure function of time. `renderFrame(t)` gives you the same pixels on
every run, which i

s why you can change one line, re-render, and diff the two —
and why rendering spreads cleanly over

change one line, re-render, and diff the two —
and why rendering spreads cleanly over a worker pool.
## A shot is a camera plus an event

The engine applies a camera around every scene, so nothing renders still by
accident. Each shot pick
s a move in its storyboard entry:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`push` `pull` `panL` `panR` `tiltUp` `tiltDown` `rollCW` `rollCCW` `arc`
`driftUp` `driftDown` `none

` are the moves. Inside the scene, three depth planes
move at different rates for parallax, the moti

f crosses the frame on `travel`, and
`stage` gives it an arc — `enter`, `drift`, `sink`, `return` —

so a song can be
told with one subject rather than six unconnected images. Beat events (rings,
kicks

, camera punches) come from the analysis, not from a hand-keyed timeline.
See docs/motion.md.
## What you draw with

A shot is either `designed` (you list elements and the engine draws them) or one
of the shipped scen

e types. `designed` is the default lane and it needs no
JavaScript:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Ten verbs (`rect` `ellipse` `line` `poly` `arc` `text` `dots` `band` `blob`
`grid`, plus `plane` and

`figure`), nine colour roles that follow the look,
per-element depth and depth-of-field, `form` sha

ding (box / cylinder / sphere),
materials (paper, grain, metal, glass, water, fabric, wood), key lig

ht with
opt-in rim light, and keyframe tracks when a thing has to *act* rather than sit.
Everything
is in docs/imagery.md.

When no arrangement of elements will do, write a scene — three lanes, cheapest
first, and the gates

gement of elements will do, write a scene — three lanes, cheapest
first, and the gates measure both:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That last one is the gate that matters most, because a still can look right and
do nothing:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Re-composing that shot with a camera push, a sinking boat and rain in the near
plane took it to `2.1

6` with every frame pair changed. `docs/scene-pipeline.md`
walks the loop.
## Lyrics are timing, not text

The fill follows the voice when the `.lrc` is word-timed
(`[00:37.67]<00:37.67>把名字从手机里 <00:39.79>悄悄删

掉了`); otherwise it falls
back to a constant reading rate. When a line's tag sits well before its fir

st
word mark, the line is shown at the *word*, not at the tag, so the text lands
with the vocal.

Most "the lyrics are off" complaints are the file, not the renderer. Streaming
exports often ship `s

ong.lrc` and `song.std.lrc`, and the `.std` variant is
derived by stamping each line with its **last

** word mark — so lines arrive late
by a different amount each time:
[该节后续省略]
### Requirements (two, both installed by you)
| dependency | version | where to get it |

| **Node.js** | ≥ 20.10 | nodejs.org — LTS release |
| **ffmpeg** | ≥ 6.0 | ffmpeg.org/download.html
— unzip, put `bin` on `PATH` |
[代码示例省略，未执行]

ffmpeg is not bundled and not downloaded for you, on purpose (see
Licensing). If it's missing, `rend

er` stops and prints the download
link for your platform instead of guessing. There's no postinstall

step and no
binary in the package.
On macOS/Linux, if `npm install` can't find Cairo/Pango headers:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What a storyboard looks like
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A few things worth knowing:

- Shots have to tile the timeline. No gaps, no overlaps, and the last `end` is
the song duration. `d

octor` checks all of it in milliseconds.
- `palette` is a mood, not a colour. The look turns `still`

, `peak`, `dawn` into
actual values: `peak` is the loudest colour the world owns. Scenes read palett

e
fields (`p.accent`, `p.text`, …), so changing the palette recolours everything.
- `enter` is how a

shot comes in. A `dissolve` inside the same set is treated as
a cut, because a dip to black mid-sce

ne is a mistake, not a transition.
- Cutting one long shot into three is normal: give the later shot

s `t0Offset`
equal to their offset inside the block and props keep their timing instead of
replaying

their entrances.
- `params` carry the copy. Every string the demo shows comes from its storyboard,
not from the engine.

Schema: docs/storyboard.md. Scenes and their parameters:
docs/scenes.md. Everything else is in
docs/
GUIDE.md, which is the one file to read first.
